result.improved_answer: First I pull the latest main into my branch so I have the most recent changes. Git then highlights the conflicting hunks with markers. I open each file, read both sides, and decide on the correct combined code—sometimes I ask the teammate who made the other change. I remove the markers, run the tests to ensure nothing broke, stage the resolved files, and commit the merge. I keep branches short and pull from main often to avoid large conflicts. During my internship I used this process to resolve a conflict in a shared config file after checking with the other developer.
